title: Dental treatment under sedation
what: You get a calming medicine and have your dental work done while relaxed and drowsy. The tooth is also numbed with a regular shot.
why: If you have a strong fear of the dentist, a strong gag reflex, or a lot of work to do in one visit.
duration: treatment usually takes 1 to 3 hours, plus rest time at the clinic afterward
tell_doctor: All your medicines and conditions, especially heart, lung, and blood pressure
Snoring or pauses in breathing during sleep
If you are or might be pregnant
Any past problems with anesthesia or sedation

prepare.title: Food and drink
prepare.text: Usually no food or drink for a few hours before sedation. The clinic will tell you the exact time.

prepare.title: Medicines
prepare.text: Do not stop your regular medicines on your own. Ask your doctor how to take them that day.

prepare.title: Someone with you
prepare.text: An adult must take you home. You cannot drive yourself.

prepare.title: Clothes
prepare.text: Comfortable clothes with short sleeves, no nail polish, no makeup.

bring: An adult to take you home
Test results, if you were asked
steps: The anesthetist or doctor asks you questions and checks your blood pressure
A sensor goes on your finger, and an IV line is placed, or the medicine is given another way
The calming medicine is given, and you relax and doze
The tooth is numbed with a shot
The dentist works while your breathing and pulse are watched the whole time
You wake up and rest at the clinic until you feel yourself again
feel: You feel calm and sleepy, and may not remember much later
The IV or gum shot is felt briefly
Afterward, you feel sleepy and weak for the rest of the day
after: Rest at home for the rest of the day
That day, do not drive, drink alcohol, or make important decisions
Do not eat until the numbness wears off
Your dentist will give you advice on tooth care
red_flags: Trouble breathing or blue lips: call emergency services
Sleepiness does not pass and the person is hard to wake: call emergency services
Severe pain or swelling where you were treated

faq.a: No. With sedation you doze, but usually breathe on your own and can respond. General anesthesia is a deeper sleep.
Treatment usually goes calmly. The tooth is also numbed with a shot.
No. You need an adult with you, and you cannot drive that day.

reminders.text: Dental treatment under sedation tomorrow. Eat and drink only until the time the clinic gave you. Arrange a ride home.
